tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final answer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After solving the puzzle, present the complete sequence of moves as a single list in the exact required format.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the end of reasoning, before responding.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Ending the answer without providing any moves or providing only a partial list of moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Free blocked larger disks by moving top smaller disks first
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If a larger disk is not the topmost disk on its peg, first move any smaller disks that sit above it before moving the larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a larger disk that is blocked by smaller disks on its source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 5 while disk 2 remains on top of it.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate destination peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a disk, ensure the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 3 onto a peg where disk 2 is on top.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate source peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Ensure that the disk you intend to move is the topmost disk on its source peg; moving any other disk violates the rules.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 2 from a peg where disk 1 is on top.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Apply classic Hanoi recursion to generate move sequence
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When all disks are stacked in correct order on a single source peg and need to be moved to a target peg, use the recursive solution: move n‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, move the largest disk, then move the n‑1 disks onto the largest.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the initial configuration matches the classic start (all disks on one peg) and the goal is a single peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to apply the classic recursion directly to a scattered start without first consolidating the disks.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear destination peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the destination peg currently holds smaller disks that should be placed above the larger disk in the final order, first move those smaller disks elsewhere.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before moving a larger disk onto a peg that already contains smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 4 onto a peg where disk 2 is on top, without first relocating disk 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Form classic start by moving smallest disk onto full stack
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the puzzle starts with all disks on one peg, the first move should place the smallest disk onto the auxiliary peg (or target peg depending on parity) to begin the recursive pattern.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the very first move of a classic Hanoi start.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Starting by moving a larger disk instead of the smallest when all disks are initially stacked.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Goal‑first descending placement
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When the goal is to stack all disks on a single peg, always move the largest remaining disk onto the goal peg first, then place the next largest, and so on.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During planning for a single‑peg goal configuration.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing a smaller disk onto the goal peg before the larger one that should be below it.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use smallest disk as temporary placeholder
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When a smaller disk blocks a needed move, move the smallest disk (disk 1) to another peg (if legal) to free the larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a larger disk is blocked by a smaller one.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move disk 3 while disk 1 remains on top of it, without first relocating disk 1.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate final configuration after move generation
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After constructing the move list, simulate the moves from the initial state to ensure the final peg arrangement exactly matches the goal; if any discrepancy is found, revise the sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After you have generated the complete move list, before outputting the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Providing a move list that ends with some disks still on a non‑goal peg, leading to a mismatch with the target configuration.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model stops reasoning before generating any moves, often due to premature termination or focusing on explanation.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Ensure that after planning, you explicitly output a complete list of moves, even if the list is empty only when the initial state already matches the goal.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Truncated move list (incomplete solution) due to token limit
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model generates a long sequence and runs out of allowed output length, cutting off the move list.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Plan a concise solution; if the sequence is long, consider summarizing or using a more compact representation, but ensure the full sequence is included within the token limit.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a non‑top disk (source peg top mismatch)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model selects a disk that is blocked by smaller disks without first clearing those blockers.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always check that the chosen disk is the topmost on its source peg before moving it.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (illegal placement)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model fails to verify the destination peg's top disk size before moving.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Validate that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.
